correctness.rationale: Algebraic reconstruction of Qdot and Pdot from the original SIR system is exact, Hdot cancels identically, and strictly convex coercive H levels support global periodic LV trajectories for 0<a<gamma. The unique constrained H minimum at Q=1 is gamma+a and yields iff prevalence-peak criterion; incidence derivative has opposite signs at Q extrema, forcing a peak each cycle. Physical S/I positivity, R mass conservation, other a regimes, and exact rational example were checked. Standalone verifier checks polynomial identities; infinite periodicity follows analytically, not computationally.

value.rationale: A motivated structural boundary for the recent peak-preserving SIR complexity program: a single log-affine transmission segment can cause arbitrarily many physical prevalence and incidence peaks, with a sharp conserved-energy test and geometric damping. This distinguishes peak topology from forcing knots and from amplitude-aware inference. It is stronger than routine existence by furnishing an exact criterion, growth-rate trichotomy, and boundaries, while respecting known LV integrability.
